nodes.label: Rejected ideas list
nodes.rationale: Rejected: protocol-named opcodes, XOR/MOV, PID hardware, auto-detect, 3R2W RF, combo uo_out, lockstep cores, PSET-fused sampling, hardware NRZI, circular imem, OUTD, ALU, protocol-select pin. True programmability is the wow.

nodes.label: Opcode is a verb, protocol is the program
nodes.norm_label: opcode is a verb, protocol is the program
nodes.rationale: Load a different listing to change protocol; Jane Street judges 'what else can this chip do', not a catalog of extra opcodes. Opcodes 1000-1111 are not spent until RX.

nodes.label: Jane Street goal: reprogrammable protocol chip
nodes.norm_label: jane street goal: reprogrammable protocol chip
nodes.rationale: A fixed UART cannot become SPI; a program that can drive, wait, shift, sample and connect/disconnect a pin can. Flexibility is what is judged.

nodes.label: Compiler pipeline (protocol dict -> asm + dmem -> hex)
nodes.norm_label: compiler pipeline (protocol dict -> asm + dmem -> hex)
nodes.rationale: NRZI, bit stuffing, CRC, LS/FS polarity are compiler work, keeping silicon dumb; listing holds dmem addresses.

nodes.label: Non-blocking IN (thought)
nodes.rationale: Deferred: 1-bit protocols cannot wait for 8 bits and dest write collides with the 1W RF; build blocking one-bit IN first.

nodes.label: Two cores (core0/core1) for independent timebases
nodes.rationale: Cores lock to their own pins; no matched pcs, no WAIT on the other core (burns power, invents a barrier). Clocked duplex on one core is sticky PSET then IN.

nodes.label: 3R1W register file (R0-R7)
nodes.rationale: Timed ops need descriptor, shifter and duration in one issue cycle; serializing reads would add clocks and break 5-clock USB FS bits. 3R2W rejected in favor of OUTM auto-refill.

nodes.label: cocotb + Icarus test suite (WSL)
nodes.rationale: A green suite can hide a bad Manchester wave; use exact run lengths (expect_runs) or a WLF dump. Tests passing != waves good.

nodes.label: Historical build order (receiver -> registers -> second protocol -> ISA)
nodes.norm_label: historical build order (receiver -> registers -> second protocol -> isa)

nodes.label: Chip vs compiler/host split of responsibility
nodes.norm_label: chip vs compiler/host split of responsibility
nodes.rationale: Chip only drives/releases/shifts/counts/jumps; packet layout, NRZI, stuffing, CRC and polarity live in the compiler/host.

nodes.label: Buffer depth (out of scope)
nodes.rationale: Queue depth is fixed in silicon; no FIFO until a workload loses a byte. SRAM macro only when storage exceeds flops.

nodes.label: EXT opcode (draft, likely 1001)
nodes.rationale: Same shape as OUT; dumps RX SRAM serially on free pins with Rd as the window, because Tiny Tapeout cannot read SRAM and dumping all uo_out while running produces garbage.

nodes.label: IN original draft (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Immediate pin / indirect dest encoding was not built; silicon IN is OUT-shaped. [1:0]=00 is the expansion joint, spent on a missing 'when', never on a protocol name.

nodes.label: RX SRAM (third 256x8 macro)
nodes.rationale: TX already owns dmem; a 1-port SRAM cannot store incoming bytes and fetch payload simultaneously, so a third SRAM is needed (supersedes dmem-from-the-back).

nodes.label: Duration Rd / hold counter
nodes.rationale: No baud generator: the listing picks N clocks per level; pins stay sticky after hold.

nodes.label: INW (IN wait-for-change mode)
nodes.rationale: For Manchester RX each mid-bit edge re-locks so sender clock error does not accumulate.

nodes.label: OUTM dmem stream refill
nodes.rationale: Refill counts 8 issues rather than Rs==0 (0x01 empties after one shift); avoids a second RF write port. Needs leftover hold >= 3.

nodes.label: USB FS ACK listing (usb_fs_ack.asm)
nodes.rationale: FS TX in scope at 5 clocks/bit; FS RX is a limitation since 5 clocks/bit cannot be software-sampled.

nodes.label: One loop shape (LD/OUT/DJNZ)
nodes.rationale: UART, SPI and USB differ only in descriptor, R3 and dmem image, not in opcode.

nodes.label: Pin input strobes (change / level-after-Rd / other-pin edge)
nodes.norm_label: pin input strobes (change / level-after-rd / other-pin edge)
nodes.rationale: RX is defined by when a uio bit enters the shift register, not by protocol; no token matching in chip.

nodes.label: Drive-only vs protocol-is-a-sample buckets
nodes.rationale: Protocols like I2C ACK, SPI MISO, JTAG TDO, SWD turnaround, PS/2, CAN ACK are pin movies without sampling; drive-only protocols can be stacked without RX.

nodes.label: SPI MOSI tax (8/8 accounting)
nodes.rationale: MOSI OUT cannot overlap a pin hold, so SCK low is shortened by MOSI_T+1 to keep 8/8 periods.
